title: Woody and Buzz Just Broke Every Record Pixar Had Left: Toy Story 5 Crosses $300 Million in 10 Days
excerpt: A $312 million global opening. The biggest animated debut of the year. And a second weekend so strong that even Pixar's doubters have gone quiet. Here's what it means — and where to watch in India.
body:
Let's get the number out of the way first, because it's absurd: **$312 million worldwide** in its opening weekend. That's $160 million domestic, $152 million international, and the kind of figure that makes studio executives weep with gratitude and competitors quietly reschedule their releases.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=c51ND9Hdbw0</youtube>

**Toy Story 5** didn't just open big. It opened like a cultural event.

Directed by **Andrew Stanton** (who gave us *Finding Nemo* and *WALL-E*) and co-directed by **Kenna Harris**, the fifth mainline *Toy Story* film brings back **Tom Hanks** as Woody, **Tim Allen** as Buzz Lightyear, and **Joan Cusack** as Jessie for a story that pits the classic toys against something every modern parent recognises: a screen.

## The Plot — and Why It Works

Bonnie has a new obsession. **Lilypad**, voiced by **Greta Lee**, is a high-tech, frog-shaped smart tablet that does everything a toy can't — stream content, answer questions, glow in the dark. The toys, suddenly irrelevant, must band together to prove that imagination still means something in a world designed to eliminate it.

It's *Toy Story* doing what *Toy Story* has always done best: wrapping genuine existential dread in bright colours and making you cry before you realise what happened. The tablet-vs-toys premise could have been preachy. Instead, it's funny, heartbreaking, and surprisingly nuanced about the way children actually engage with technology — not as villains, but as kids doing what kids do.



> **"## The Box Office Is Historic

The $160 million domestic opening is the best in *Toy Story* franchise history, surpassing *Toy Story 4*'s $120.9 million launch in 2019."**


## The Box Office Is Historic

The $160 million domestic opening is the best in *Toy Story* franchise history, surpassing *Toy Story 4*'s $120.9 million launch in 2019. It's the second-biggest animated opening ever in the US, behind only *Incredibles 2*. And it's the strongest opening weekend of any film in 2026 so far.

But here's the number that matters most: the **second weekend drop**. *Toy Story 5* is projected to earn approximately **$72.5 million** in its sophomore frame — a drop of just 54%. That's exceptional for a film that opened this high, and it pushed the cumulative domestic total past **$300 million in just 10 days**.


![Buzz Lightyear — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/0/02/Buzz_Lightyear_sculpture_of_Toy_Story_Hotel_Shanghai_%28cropped%29.jpg)


For context: *Toy Story 3* and *Toy Story 4* both took until their third weekends to reach that milestone. Neither the original *Toy Story* ($237 million lifetime) nor *Toy Story 2* ($245 million lifetime) ever got there at all.

## How It's Playing in India

In India, *Toy Story 5* has collected approximately **₹9.25 crore** at the box office through its first nine days, across English, Hindi, and dubbed versions. The opening weekend brought in ₹6 crore, with Chennai, Mumbai, and Bengaluru leading occupancy.

Those aren't blockbuster numbers by Indian standards — this was always going to be a niche play compared to *Cocktail 2* and *Welcome To The Jungle* — but for a Hollywood animated film in a month crowded with Bollywood heavyweights, it's a respectable showing. The film's audience skews toward urban, English-speaking families and the nostalgia-driven millennial crowd who grew up with Woody and Buzz in the '90s.

For diaspora audiences, *Toy Story 5* is currently in theatres across the **US, UK, Canada, Australia**, and most major markets. In India, it's running in **IMAX, 3D, and standard formats** across multiplexes.

## Why the Doubters Were Wrong

Before release, the narrative around *Toy Story 5* was sceptical. *Toy Story 4* had given the franchise a perfect ending — Woody said goodbye, handed over the badge, and walked into the sunset. Did we really need another one?

Pixar's answer, backed by $312 million in opening-weekend receipts and a 54% second-weekend hold, is unambiguous: yes, if the story justifies it. The tablet premise isn't a gimmick — it's the natural evolution of what *Toy Story* has always been about. What happens when the thing you were made for doesn't need you anymore?

The reviews have been strong (not *Toy Story 3*-level rapturous, but solidly warm), audiences are bringing their kids, and the legs suggest this will run deep into July.

## What's Next

*Toy Story 5* faces its first real competition this coming week as **Supergirl** enters the market, though the DC film's $38 million debut suggests Woody and Buzz won't be losing sleep. The bigger question is whether it can sustain its pace to challenge $500 million domestic — a threshold no animated film has ever reached without a re-release.

For now, Pixar has done what it does best: made you feel something about plastic toys with sewn-on smiles. And this time, 10 days and $300 million later, the world is still feeling it.
